name: default
_comment: The shipped look. Every pixel value here was measured off a reference
screenshot of the target frame, not invented -- see 'Deriving a look' in
the README for the one-factor method, which is how you redo these for your
A preset is merged over the built-in default, so you only need the keys you
change: a file containing just {"captions": {"font_px": 64}} is valid.
Run with --canvas WxH to scale every pixel value uniformly; a canvas of a
different ASPECT is an error rather than a silent stretch.
_main: The fragment window, in canvas pixels. Its aspect decides the source crop:
the source is centre-cropped to 1056:960 = 1.1 and scaled to exactly this
box. That is NOT a 16:9 fit (a 16:9 fit at 1056 wide would be 594 tall) --
the frame is scaled to the window's height and the sides are cropped.
_bg: The same frame cover-scaled to the whole canvas from the SOURCE'S OWN
aspect, blurred, and multiplied down. darken is a multiply: out = in * 0.5.
Do not express this as a brightness offset -- that is subtractive and
crushes dark scenes to pure black.
_captions: strip_y/strip_h is the region pass 2 overlays. Keeping it 1080x300 instead
of a whole frame is what keeps the overlay at ~15 s instead of minutes.
top is measured inside the strip, so the cap line lands at canvas y 1360.
min_hold is a requested floor within each SRT cue; it is reduced when
n_lines * min_hold > cue_duration, preserving pauses between cues.
_font: null -> search the usual font directories for a heavy display face.
Set an absolute path here, or pass --font, to pin one.
